subject: Dedicated capacity: flexible reservation structures for VentureMed

Subject: Drafting flexible reservation options for VentureMed

Maya,

Quick note before you send the proposal: VentureMed asked specifically for a structure that lets them ramp capacity up quickly in Q4 but avoid a large minimum spend early. Can you draft 2–3 options that vary on (1) committed minimum GPUs, (2) staged ramp schedule, and (3) a short-term burst pool? Keep an option that has an early-exit clause at month 6 tied to usage thresholds.

Also flag any SLA/availability impacts if the minimum is below 8 GPUs. I'm happy to review.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@venturemed.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@venturemed.com>, procurement@venturemed.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:18:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity: flexible reservation structures for VentureMed

Alex / Sara —

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Per our conversation, attached are three committed-reservation options we think will map to your product roadmap and budget cycles. Short summary below; see attached PDF and cost spreadsheet for line-by-line math.

Option A — Conservative starter
- Minimum commitment: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Ramp: maintain 6 GPUs months 1–3, add +4 GPUs month 4, review at month 6
- Burst pool: 20% convertible burst credits available up to +2 GPUs for short windows
- Early-exit: allowed at month 6 if 30-day rolling usage < 40% of committed baseline
- Notes: lowest upfront cost; higher per-token unit price under load

Option B — Balanced scale (recommended)
- Minimum commitment: 10 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Ramp: 10 GPUs months 1–2, +6 GPUs month 3, +6 GPUs month 6 (phased to 22)
- Burst pool: 30% burst credits; priority scheduling during regional capacity
- Early-exit: buy-down to 8 GPUs at month 6 with pro-rated credit
- Notes: balanced latency/cost; fits predicted Q4 growth curve

Option C — Aggressive reserve
- Minimum commitment: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Ramp: 20 GPUs day 1, sustained; optional autoscale to +30 GPUs via reserved burst
- Burst pool: dedicated reserved headroom for predictable latency
- Early-exit: none (discounts tied to full-year commitment)
- Notes: lowest unit cost, highest commitment and SLA guarantees

Attachments: venturemed_dedicated_options_v1.pdf, cost_breakdown_3_scenarios.xlsx

Next steps: if you prefer, we can convert Option B into a phased purchase order that aligns milestones to product launches. Let me know which option you want us to put into a formal SOW.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Lead, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Li <alex.li@venturemed.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@venturemed.com>, procurement@venturemed.com
Date: 2027-06-21T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: flexible reservation structures for VentureMed

Maya —

Thanks, that format is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:
1) Our product team expects a spike in inference load around Nov 1; flexibility to burst up quickly (within 10 minutes) is critical. Is the burst pool designed for instant provisioning or will there be queueing behind other customers?
2) Can we move the early-exit trigger in Option A to month 4 instead of month 6 if we hit a usage shortfall?
3) For Option B, what latency SLOs can you guarantee at 22 GPUs in the US-east region? We need a P95 < 180ms for 4k tokens.

Also send me a sample SOW clause for the early-exit and for how you account for preempted hardware during regional capacity events.

—Alex
VP Product, VentureMed

---
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@venturemed.com>
Cc: Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@venturemed.com>, procurement@venturemed.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: flexible reservation structures for VentureMed

Alex —

Great questions, answers inline: 
1) Burst pool behavior: our burst pool for Dedicated reservations is backed by reserved headroom in the same regional cluster when possible. For Option B the 30% burst credits are implemented as pre-warmed slots that can start within ~60–120 seconds in normal conditions; under regional contention they may queue with degraded priority. We can offer an SLA-backed fast-burst add-on (additional monthly fee) that guarantees <15s spin-up by reserving hot standbys.

2) Early-exit timing: we can make the early-exit test for Option A at month 4 instead of month 6, but it changes the pricing: the early-exit buyback rate would be less favorable (we'd apply a 25% buyback premium vs 15% at month 6) to account for capacity planning risk.

3) Latency SLOs: for the US-east cluster and 4k-token workloads, at 22 GPUs we can commit P95 < 180ms with the following caveats: 1) batching configuration in production must follow the recommendations in the attached PDF; 2) KV/prefix caching must be enabled for the endpoints serving LLM inference; 3) if you enable large-scale concurrent long-context sessions (100+ concurrent 4k sessions) we should increase baseline to 28 GPUs to keep P95 headroom.

I've attached a short SOW clause (see PDF page 4) for early-exit language and a short paragraph describing preemption/region contention handling.

If you want the <15s guaranteed burst we can include it as Option B+. I can send a redline SOW by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Maya

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@venturemed.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: flexible reservation structures for VentureMed

Alex / VentureMed team —

Appreciate the level of detail here. Two follow-ups from our side:
1) If you anticipate aggressive Q4 growth, we recommend Option B with the Option B+ burst add-on and the month-4 early-exit (with adjusted buyback). That combo gives you fast burst, predictable SLA, and a mid-term safety valve.
2) We'll include an onboarding checklist (networking, KMS, audit logs) in the SOW and a 30-day performance review milestone tied to ramp triggers.

I'll have legal send a starter SOW redline after Maya shares the marked-up language. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call next week to align procurement and product.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
